classification.difficultyReason: Extract event probabilities from region frequencies and verify the independence criterion.

content.prompt: Events $A$ and $B$ are shown in the Venn diagram. Show that $A$ and $B$ are independent.

spec.description: Unshaded overlapping circles A and B inside a rectangular sample space. Ordinary source-blue outlines are rendered black under house style.
spec.mathematics: Region frequencies: A only 9, intersection 6, B only 10, neither 15; total 40.
spec.answerVisibility: All four frequencies and both event labels are permanent givens.

answer.worked:
The total frequency is $9+6+10+15=40$.
$$\begin{align*}P(A)&=\frac{9+6}{40}=\frac{3}{8}\\P(B)&=\frac{6+10}{40}=\frac{2}{5}\\P(A\cap B)&=\frac{6}{40}=\frac{3}{20}\\P(A)\times P(B)&=\frac{3}{8}\times\frac{2}{5}=\frac{3}{20}.\end{align*}$$
Since $P(A\cap B)=P(A)\times P(B)$, events $A$ and $B$ are independent.
